recall.minute: Every RL algorithm can be placed by five questions: what it learns (values, action values, policy, model), where its targets come from (expected backups, sampled returns, bootstrapped estimates), whether it uses a model, whether it bootstraps, and how data are generated (on-policy, off-policy, logged, simulated). The Bellman recursion links DP (known model), TD and Q-learning (samples), DQN (networks with replay and target networks), actor–critic (values guiding a policy) and planning (simulated experience). State, reward, return and value must stay distinct. Bandits isolate exploration; DP plans; MC averages returns; TD bootstraps; SARSA, Expected SARSA and Q-learning differ only in their next-action term. Worked TD error: 2 + 0.9 × 1.5 − 1.0 = 2.35, usable by critic and actor. Policy gradients share the form Δθ ∝ signal × ∇log π (return, advantage or TD error); PPO clips ratios; RLHF, DPO and GRPO adapt this to LLMs. Three independent axes: model-based/free, value/policy-based, on/off-policy (DQN value/off; PPO policy/on; MCTS model-based planning). Formulate the problem (agents, state, actions, reward, horizon, data, model, output, constraints, evaluation) before choosing an algorithm.
